title: Console parsimony cutset — acceptance matrix for dashboards/tracing/costs
creator: Asha Mehta
description: Prune Console surface to a defensible minimal MVP across dashboards, tracing, and route-level cost breakdown so we can ship a reliable alpha with bounded effort and operating cost. This ticket captures the acceptance matrix, trade-offs for feature removal, fallback behavior, rollout gating, and measurement plan. It is intentionally opinionated: prioritize actionable SRE/SEV signals and top-3 customer scenarios over full fidelity visualizations.
scope_in:
- Route-level top-line cost card (single numeric + delta) for top 10 routes by spend
- Essential trace view: flamegraph with 1 sampled span per request and 3 filtering dimensions (route, model, status)
- Latency P95/P99 per route card (30-day rolling)
- Telemetry sampling: 1% default with opt-in 10% for smoke customers
- Rollout controls: feature flag + canary cohort (10% orgs)
- Acceptance telemetry for rollout: error rate, dashboard load time, memory footprint
scope_out:
- Full trace waterfall with step-by-step payloads and per-token timing
- Per-token cost attribution and token-level cost breakdowns
- Unlimited route listing and complex filtering UX
- Real-time streaming of traces and live tailing
- Long-term raw-span retention beyond 7 days in alpha
decision_log:
2025-02-10: PM+Eng+Design agreed to reduce trace fidelity to a sampled flamegraph to save infra cost (meeting notes: https://confluence.redwood.ai/Console/compact-trace-decision)
2025-02-18: Opted for 'route-first' surface instead of 'model-first' after customer interviews with two early access partners (notes attached)
2025-02-24: Scoped telemetry sampling to 1% default to meet cost SLOs; provided opt-in pathway for QA orgs
tradeoffs:
- Lower trace fidelity reduces root-cause detail but preserves lightweight failure detection.
- Sampling prevents exact per-customer cost attribution but keeps hosting costs manageable for alpha.
- Minimal cards reduce discoverability for power users; mitigated by clear 'more details' CTAs and a roadmap to expand in GA.
acceptance_criteria: Dashboard: Route cost card shows top 10 routes by spend with numeric cost + 24h delta; data latency <= 5 minutes for aggregated metrics
Tracing: Trace view opens and displays sampled flamegraph for a selected request within 2s for 95% of requests in staging; filtering by route/model/status returns results within 3s
Telemetry: Default sampling at 1% enforced; account-level opt-in toggle increases to 10% and is honored within one hour
Performance: New UI load does not increase console median page load by >200ms in canary cohort
Reliability: No more than 0.5% increase in error budget consumption for the hosting cluster during rollout
Rollout: Feature flag gated to 10% canary and automated rollback triggers on: (a) trace ingestion pipeline error rate >1% sustained for 5m, (b) dashboard 95th pctile load time regression >500ms
Observability: Dashboards emit instrumentation events for adoption (view, filter, opt-in) and a Grafana board exists for rollout metrics
